name: nuclear revival
statements: b0
A lawsuit challenging decisions in the Palisades Nuclear Power Plant restart effort was dismissed by a judge.
b1
Utilities surveyed by the Nuclear Energy Institute are planning for 33.6 gigawatts of new nuclear generation over the next 15 years.
b2

The Department of Energy's Reactor Pilot Program allows companies to bypass the Nuclear Regulatory Commission's traditional licensing process, with oversight placed under the Energy Department instead.
b3
The current wave of reactor start-ups and criticality announcements represents a rebirth of America's nuclear industry.
b4
Reduced regulatory oversight through the Department of Energy Reactor Pilot Program enabled companies to achieve reactor criticality in less than one year.
b5
Most existing nuclear reactors in the United States will continue operating for at least 80 years from their initial construction dates.
b6
The United States has been right to avoid commercial use of plutonium for five decades to prevent nuclear weapons proliferation.
b7
The United States should streamline its nuclear regulatory process to enable faster reactor construction.
b8
Valar Atomics achieved criticality on June 18, 2026, producing heat from a reactor core in the Utah desert.
b9
Nine of the ten nuclear reactors whose construction began worldwide in 2025 were located in China.
A 1976 California law bans the construction of new nuclear power plants in the state.
The plan to let private firms use plutonium as fuel reverses a decades-long US policy of avoiding commercial use of plutonium to prevent weapons proliferation.
Artificial intelligence infrastructure demand is driving utilities to plan new nuclear generation capacity over the coming years.
The Duane Arnold nuclear plant in Iowa will resume operations by 2029.
Achieving rapid nuclear reactor development through streamlined regulatory approval is a positive achievement for American energy independence.
The federal government should continue providing loans to support the restart of previously shut down nuclear power plants.
Antares Nuclear's Mark-0 reactor completed a zero-power fueled criticality demonstration at Idaho National Laboratory on June 4, 2026.
The United States has nearly 100,000 metric tons of used nuclear fuel stored around the country.
President Trump's May 2025 executive order set a deadline of July 4, 2026, for at least three new experimental nuclear reactors to reach criticality.
Small modular reactors represent a new technological approach that differs significantly from traditional large nuclear power plants.
Concerns about plutonium proliferation and weapons security are causing opponents to challenge the government's decision to make surplus plutonium available to private companies.
Small modular reactors deployed on barges will power coastal ports and maritime operations within the coming years.
Restarting previously shuttered nuclear plants is a beneficial use of America's energy assets.
The Nuclear Regulatory Commission's traditional licensing process should be sidestepped for new small reactor designs to speed up deployment.
